primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Primary generalized glucocorticoid resistance (Chrousos syndrome) due to NR3C1 dysfunction
mechanism: Reduced glucocorticoid-receptor signaling weakens cortisol-mediated negative feedback at the hypothalamus and pituitary, increasing CRH/ACTH drive and cortisol production. ACTH also increases adrenal mineralocorticoid-active steroids and androgens, producing hypertension/hypokalemia and hyperandrogenic manifestations without classic Cushingoid features.
vignette: A 20-year-old woman is evaluated for hypertension, acne, and hirsutism. She has no central obesity, proximal muscle weakness, easy bruising, or violaceous striae. Serum cortisol is markedly elevated and plasma ACTH is elevated. Potassium is low. Genetic testing identifies a loss-of-function pathogenic variant in NR3C1.
lead: Which of the following physiologic changes most directly explains the persistent elevation of ACTH in this patient?
correct: Reduced glucocorticoid-mediated negative feedback at the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary
distractors: Autonomous ACTH secretion by a pituitary corticotroph adenoma
Increased cortisol-binding globulin causing elevation of measured total cortisol
Increased renal conversion of cortisol to cortisone by 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2
Increased sensitivity of hypothalamic glucocorticoid receptors to circulating cortisol
distractor_notes: A corticotroph adenoma can raise ACTH, but the vignette directly identifies loss of glucocorticoid-receptor function; impaired receptor-mediated feedback explains the compensatory ACTH elevation and the absence of typical Cushingoid findings.
Higher cortisol-binding globulin can raise total cortisol without producing the glucocorticoid-resistance pattern of elevated ACTH, mineralocorticoid-active steroid effects, and hyperandrogenism.
11β-HSD2 inactivates cortisol in mineralocorticoid target tissues; increased activity does not explain loss of central glucocorticoid feedback and compensatory ACTH elevation.
Increased receptor sensitivity would strengthen glucocorticoid negative feedback and suppress ACTH, the opposite of this disorder.
key_expl: NR3C1 loss of function reduces tissue responsiveness to cortisol. In the hypothalamus and pituitary this weakens glucocorticoid negative feedback, so CRH and ACTH rise and drive compensatory hypercortisolism. Because mineralocorticoid-active steroids and adrenal androgens also increase, patients may develop hypertension, hypokalemia, and hyperandrogenism despite lacking typical Cushingoid features.
objective: Explain primary generalized glucocorticoid resistance as impaired glucocorticoid-receptor feedback causing compensatory CRH/ACTH activation and hypercortisolism without Cushingoid features.
